content:
Build a full character bible (name, body build, kit color, kit number, hairstyle) and lock it before generating any Seedance 2.0 shots to prevent character drift.

Create a single turnaround sheet (front, 3/4 front, side, 3/4 back, back) and use it as the character reference instead of relying on one portrait.

Include an expression sheet (focused, determined, mid-sprint, goal celebration, smirk) in the reference pack to keep facial/emotional consistency across shots.

Add an action-pose sheet (standing, sprinting, shooting, aerial, victory) so Seedance animates consistent body mechanics in every clip.

Specify kit details with exact hex color codes (shirt/shorts/socks + stripe pattern) to keep numbers and patterns from changing between scenes.

Feed the finished character sheet/bible into Seedance 2.0 as a hard character reference for all generations.

Generate clips in match-narrative order (stadium intro → final shot) and stitch them in that sequence to maintain continuity.

For wide stadium/crowd shots where the face drifts, regenerate that shot until the character matches the locked reference.
